- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later days.
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 69.51 or 70+), then fails to correct downward.
- Underestimates mean-reverting periods — model holds too low when recent history shows strong upward momentum.
- Forecasts tend to lag behind true price movements by 3–7 days, especially in the 15–25 day range.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices in the 20–30 day forecast window, especially when history includes recent highs.
- When history contains a strong upward trend, model fails to fully capture the momentum, underestimating the peak.
- Model often fails to adjust for seasonal or calendar-driven volatility (e.g., December spikes) — overestimates early, underestimates late.
- Forecasts show a tendency to “smooth” volatility — underestimates sharp drops and overestimates gradual rises.
- Model exhibits “memory decay” — recent history (last 5–7 days) is underweighted in forecasting, leading to lagged responses.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in early days, model tends to overcorrect later, causing downward bias.
